---
title: "09 — Assess missingness and geographic change"
output: html_notebook
---

**Measures:** how the 2025 subgroup model behaves when income or other predictors are missing, and whether differences persist in jurisdictions appearing in both 2024 and 2025. These analyses diagnose selection and coverage risks; they do not eliminate nonresponse bias.


## Setup

Loads the unchanged input settings, shared model functions, and the persistent run
increment. The output suffix identifies this run.

```{r setup}
# Set the project root, then load R code from the shared R Notebooks.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Project-root discovery
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Search upward for the project marker so notebook paths do not depend on a particular
# subfolder.
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
    current <- normalizePath(start, mustWork = TRUE)
    # Walk toward the filesystem root until the project marker is found.
    repeat {
        if (file.exists(file.path(current, "FMD_Project.Rproj"))) {
            return(current)
        }
        # Move up one directory; an unchanged parent marks the filesystem root.
        parent <- dirname(current)
        if (identical(parent, current)) {
            stop("Open FMD_Project.Rproj in RStudio first")
        }
        current <- parent
    }
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Notebook execution root
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Resolve the project before loading modules; configure subsequent knitr chunks to use
# that root.
project_root <- find_project_root()
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared-module loader
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Extract R chunks in source order and evaluate them in the caller environment.
# This lightweight loader does not process chunk options such as eval = FALSE.
load_module <- function(name) {
    path <- file.path(project_root, "R", paste0(name, ".Rmd"))
    text <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
    starts <- which(startsWith(text, "```{r"))
    ends <- which(trimws(text) == "```")
    blocks <- lapply(starts, function(start) {
        # Use the next standalone closing fence for this R chunk.
        finish <- ends[ends > start][1]
        if (is.na(finish) || finish <= start + 1L) {
            stop("Missing code or closing fence in ", path)
        }
        paste(text[(start + 1L):(finish - 1L)], collapse = "\n")
    })
    eval(parse(text = paste(blocks, collapse = "\n\n")), envir = parent.frame())
    invisible(TRUE)
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared settings and utilities
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Load configuration before helpers, retaining the existing presentation palette module.
load_module("config")
load_module("run_manager")
load_module("helpers")
load_module("plot_palette")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Existing-run attachment
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Attach to an allocated run rather than incrementing the counter in this stage.
run_context <- attach_run()
cat("[RUN] Current increment:", run_context$id, "\n")
```


## Audit missing predictors and performance

Calculates the prevalence of missing encoded predictors and the selected model’s
performance separately in records with observed versus any missing predictor.

```{r audit-missing-predictors-and-performance}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Missingness and model performance
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Identify explicit Missing categories without treating them as observed responses.
# Missingness rates here are unweighted; performance metrics use survey weights.

scored <- load_run_rds("checkpoints", "07_scored_2025")
scored[, missing_any := apply(
    as.data.frame(.SD),
    1,
    function(row) any(row == "Missing")
), .SDcols = feature_names]

missing_by_group <- scored[, .(
    respondents = .N,
    missing_any_rate = mean(missing_any),
    missing_income_rate = mean(INCOME_BAND == "Missing"),
    unknown_outcome_rate = mean(!valid_outcome(FMD))
), by = cohort]

# Save this result under the attached run ID so it remains linked to the current
# analysis.
save_table(missing_by_group, "09_missingness_by_group")
print(missing_by_group)

performance <- scored[
    cohort %in% primary_groups & valid_outcome(FMD),
    as.list(weighted_metrics(FMD, selected_probability, RAW_WEIGHT)),
    by = .(cohort, missing_any)
]

# Save this result under the attached run ID so it remains linked to the current
# analysis.
save_table(performance, "09_missingness_performance")
print(performance)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Visualization
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------


# Build the chart using the existing palette and theme; retain the original scales and
# labels.
plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    missing_by_group,
    ggplot2::aes(reorder(cohort, missing_any_rate), missing_any_rate, fill = cohort)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_col() +
    ggplot2::coord_flip() +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
    atg_scale_fill_groups() +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "2025 respondents with at least one missing predictor",
        x = "Recorded population category",
        y = "Unweighted share of survey responses"
    )
show_and_save(plot, "09_missing_predictor_prevalence", 9, 5)
```


## Test common-geography sensitivity

Compares the same 2025 model within states represented in 2024 and 2025. This holds the
set of states constant, but not their sample composition or nonresponse.

```{r test-common-geography-sensitivity}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Common-state sensitivity analysis
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Hold the represented state set constant between 2024 and 2025.
# This restriction does not hold respondent composition or response behavior constant.

historical <- read_historical()
states_2024 <- unique(historical[YEAR == 2024L, STATE])
states_2025 <- unique(scored$STATE)
common_states <- intersect(states_2024, states_2025)

common_test <- scored[
    STATE %in% common_states & cohort %in% primary_groups & valid_outcome(FMD)
]
rows <- list()

# Iterate through the configured analysis items in the original execution order.
for (group in primary_groups) {
    data <- common_test[cohort == group]
    rows[[group]] <- data.frame(
        cohort = group,
        coverage = "common_states_2024_2025",
        states = length(common_states),
        weighted_metrics(data$FMD, data$selected_probability, data$RAW_WEIGHT)
    )
}
results <- data.table::rbindlist(rows)

# Save this result under the attached run ID so it remains linked to the current
# analysis.
save_table(data.frame(STATE = common_states), "09_common_state_ids")
save_table(results, "09_common_geography_metrics")
print(results)
```
